findings.title: Fallback locales are only loaded for HTTP requests; jobs, mailers and rake tasks cannot fall back
findings.body: The fallback chain ([current locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en]) is only materialized on disk in ApplicationController#set_locale via the new I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! call. The translate accelerator loads translations lazily per locale: I18n.translate only calls load_locale(config.locale), and nothing outside the controller (Sidekiq jobs, ActionMailer such as notification/digest emails, rake tasks, console) ever loads the fallback locales. So when a key is missing in the user's locale in one of those contexts, the I18n::Backend::Fallbacks module iterates the fallback chain but the backend holds no data for the default locale or :en (their yml files were never read), and the output is "translation missing: ..." instead of the English text. This is exactly the case the feature is meant to fix, and emails are a primary surface for it. The ensure_loaded! call should live in the translation path itself (e.g. have I18n.ensure_loaded!/load_locale load the whole fallback chain for the locale) or be invoked from job/mailer entry points, not solely from ApplicationController.

findings.title: Translation LRU cache key ignores SiteSetting.default_locale, which now affects resolved values
findings.body: Translations are cached under a key of key + config.locale + backend.object_id, but with the new FallbackLocaleList the value returned by translate_no_cache also depends on SiteSetting.default_locale (the middle entry of the fallback chain). If an admin changes the site's default locale at runtime, entries already cached through the old chain are never invalidated — the accelerator's @cache is only cleared by I18n.reload!, which a site-setting change does not trigger — so users can keep seeing fallback text in the previous default language until the 300-entry LRU happens to evict those keys or the process restarts. Include the default locale in the cache key or clear the translation cache when default_locale changes.

findings.title: No specs cover the new fallback resolution and loading behavior
findings.body: This PR changes how every missing translation is resolved (custom FallbackLocaleList ordering user locale -> SiteSetting.default_locale -> :en, fallbacks now enabled in all environments instead of only production, and explicit per-locale loading via ensure_loaded!), yet adds no tests. At minimum there should be coverage that a key missing in the current locale resolves to the site default locale and then to English, and that ensure_loaded! loads each locale in the chain, since regressions here surface as user-visible "translation missing" strings across the site and in emails.
